title: mini field scan: quant telescope - latency/quality probes
content:
Context and goal:

Quick exploratory sweep (mini field scan) to surface short-path failure modes and kernel-level interactions when running mixed quant variants (AWQ, GPTQ, int8 reference kernels) on mid-size workloads. This is intentionally lightweight: narrow set of models, concise probes, and microprofiling hooks so we can decide whether to escalate to a broader bench.

Why "telescope"?
- Probe short-duration, rare but high-impact events (p95/p99 latency spikes, tail jitter) by zooming into a live-ish workload using higher sampling frequency and KV-prefetch toggles.

Experiment summary (what I ran):
- Models: tuned run on two model families: Llama2-13B and a trimmed open-llm-30B replica used for internal compatibility tests.
- Variants: baseline FP16, AWQ-INT8 (our AWQ pipeline + userland packing), GPTQ-4bit-approx (as delivered by q4_0-like artifact), and a reference native int8-kernel we maintain in runtime.
- Hardware: A100-40GB (single-GPU) and T4 cluster node (for representative edge-like behavior).
- Workload: 5k replayed short chats (avg prompt 45 tokens, response cap 128 tokens) and a bursty mix: 80% short (<=32 tokens) / 20% long.
- Harness: telescope-v2 harness (lightweight python runner with perf hooks: nvprof traces (short capture), kernel timelines, per-token latency histograms, and a KV-prefetch toggle).
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency per request, token throughput, kernel-level occupancy, L2 dram eviction counts (where available), perplexity on heldout set, and downstream QA exact-match on 200 examples.

Top-line observations (concise):
1) AWQ-INT8 gives ~1.9x token throughput vs FP16 for short responses, but p99 shows 1.8–2.3x jitter increases depending on kernel packing.
2) GPTQ variant is slightly faster than AWQ on long sequences (>=128 tokens) on A100 but underperforms on T4 due to a suboptimal kernel fallback path.
3) The reference int8 kernel had the lowest per-token CPU pre/post-processing overhead but exhibited a distinct tail pattern: sporadic 30–80ms spikes correlated with tile-eviction events.
4) KV-prefetch enabled reduced mean latency by 6–12% for AWQ on A100 but had marginal or negative impact on T4 for small prompts because of L2 thrash.

Microprofiling notes (what the telescope found):
- Tile eviction oscillation: when batch size is small and response lengths variable, we saw repeated allocation/eviction cycles in the tiled matmul path (our allocator stats + trace). Evictions line up with kernel swaps (fast int8 -> slower gptq path) and cause multi-millisecond stalls.
- Launch overhead vs compute: on the T4, the AWQ small-kernel launches dominate for short tokens (launch+warmup >> compute). On A100, compute dominates but the packing/unpacking stage shows CPU-side jitter when the runtime serializes certain cache operations.
- Bank contention: A100 L2 counters show hotspotting on banks when kernel microtiles are misaligned (stride mismatch). This is most visible on sequences with token-length variance (10–128) within the same microbatch.
- Memory copy patterns: AWQ packing writes into temporary buffers that are often page-crossing; the scatter pattern sometimes triggers extra cudaMemcpy host-device page pinning overheads in our test harness (we mitigated temporarily with a bigger pinned-pool).

Quality tradeoffs (small heldout checks):
- AWQ-INT8: small QA drop vs FP16 (~1.8 EM points on the 200-sample check), but often indistinguishable for conversational fluency. Some failure classes: numerics in code blocks, long-run co-reference when sequence >160 tokens.
- GPTQ-approx: slightly higher variance in generation (2.4 EM drop) but less systematic bias on numeric transforms.
- Reference int8 kernel: quality almost identical to AWQ for short sequences but shows catastrophic token hallucinations occasionally on long recursions (>300 tokens) in the trimmed 30B replica.

Concrete perf numbers (representative slice):
- Llama2-13B, A100, short chat workload (avg response 48 tokens):
  - FP16: throughput 7.8 tok/s, p95 latency 210ms, p99 420ms
  - AWQ-INT8: throughput 14.6 tok/s, p95 260ms, p99 630ms
  - GPTQ: throughput 12.2 tok/s, p95 300ms, p99 580ms
  - ref-int8: throughput 15.1 tok/s, p95 230ms, p99 710ms
Notes: ref-int8 spikes tied to eviction events; AWQ higher p99 due to packing serialization.

Hypotheses (what might be causing these patterns):
1) Packing serialization: our AWQ packing path uses a global write lock for some buffer pools to reduce fragmentation; at bursty arrival patterns the lock becomes a contention point and elongates p99.
2) Kernel selection hysteresis: when the scheduler switches kernels based on recent latency vs throughput, it sometimes flips back-and-forth on borderline loads, causing repeated slow path invocations.
3) L2 bank striding: kernel microtile shapes from AWQ packing sometimes produce bank-aligned hotspots; remapping tiles could smooth access.
4) T4 path fallback: a non-optimized memcpy path in qconv on T4 triggers small-copy overheads; need a fast-path for small contiguous writes.

Short-term remediation experiments to try next (planned):
- Remove global pack write lock and test per-thread arenas (small A/B). Potential downside: increased fragmentation—monitor memory growth.
- Introduce a short cooldown hysteresis when switching kernels to avoid flip-flop in selection (config knob: kernel_cooldown_ms = 200).
- Microtile remap: try alternate packing strides to avoid bank hotspots; run L2 bank heatmap on A100.
- T4 small-copy fast-path: implement an inlined memcpy vector for small contiguous AWQ writes to avoid page pin penalties.

Observability improvements (quick wins):
- Add explicit "pack-lock-wait" trace span and expose histogram in console for the AWQ pack path.
- Emit kernel-selection events with reason codes (capacity|latency|fallback) so rollouts can be analyzed post-mortem.
- KV-prefetch telemetry: log prefetch hit/miss and the corresponding per-request latency delta (so we can correlate when prefetch helps/hurts).

Notes to engineering readers (gotchas & current limitations):
- The harness uses short nvprof captures (1s) to keep overhead low; this hides long tail single-event artifacts. If we escalate, use longer CUPTI traces for the p99 cases.
- The trimmed 30B replica is not our canonical customer model; behavior may differ with other weights/architectures (e.g., FlashAttention variants).
- Some of the failure modes only manifest at certain PRNG seeds (we saw one pattern disappear when using deterministic allocator seeds).

Decisions and asks:
- Priority: medium. AWQ gives net cost wins but p99 wobble is customer-visible; prefer mitigations that don't compromise throughput.
- Ask infra: enable a dedicated small pinned pool on the playground A100 nodes for repeatable AWQ tests (tickets: JIRA-RT-1302).
- Ask perf infra: schedule a 2h deep-capture session (CUPTI + kernel timeline) on A100 with the long-chat workload to capture root cause of the 600–800ms p99 spikes.

Next steps (who will do what):
- Asha: implement pack-lock per-thread arena toy patch and run quick smoke on A100 (timeline: 3 days).
- Marco: add kernel-selection reason codes to trace spans (timeline: 2 days).
- Lena: prepare CUPTI capture job and L2 bank heatmaps (timeline: 5 days).
- Devon: prototype small-copy fast-path on T4 (timeline: 1 week).

Appendix: quick logs and artifacts (snippets)
- Example request trace showing pack-lock stall: [trace id: tt-20260118-31] (see PR #4821 for instrumentation)
- Short nvprof excerpt: kernel blast aligned at 23.4ms cycles, followed by 58ms idle wait at pack stage (screenshot saved in perf-run-2026-01-18).

Loose to-do and questions (brain-dump):
- Should we prefer AWQ variant for Dedicated customers by default and gate prefetch? Or make prefetch adaptive per-hardware profile?
- If per-thread arenas increase fragmentation too much, consider an intermediate pooled-lock with per-MB locking granularity.
- Run the same sweep against a 65B-ish family in the next quarter to validate scaling behavior.

If you want the raw harness scripts, I put them under the perf playground repo branch: github.com/redwood-inference/perf-playground/tree/mini-quant-telescope.

— Asha
